scope: Two source-grounded literature notes linked to existing public reaction–enzyme associations. Separate from the frozen assay database and its assertion counts.
review_method: AI-assisted extraction and targeted primary-text checks, with exact native-sequence comparison to current UniProt and the paper-listed RefSeq accession.

records.reaction_context: Cinnamate to cinnamaldehyde; ATP- and NADPH-dependent carboxylate reduction.
records.assay_readout: NADPH loss at 340 nm. The paper additionally reports cinnamaldehyde formation by HPLC; that pH-confirmation trace is described as data not shown.
records.product_confirmation: Product formation is reported by the authors using HPLC; the specific pH-confirmation trace is not displayed.
records.construct: Codon-optimized NcCAR, expressed with an N-terminal TEV-cleavable His tag and coexpressed E. coli phosphopantetheinyltransferase. Kinetic parameters were determined after His-tag cleavage and further purification.

conditions.description: MES buffer prepared at 100 mM with 10 mM MgCl2; 160 µL buffer in a 200 µL reaction, ATP and NADPH supplied, 5% v/v DMSO. The stock buffer concentrations are not asserted as the final assay concentrations.

paper.title: Selective Enzymatic Transformation to Aldehydes in vivo by Fungal Carboxylate Reductase from Neurospora crassa

limitations: These parameters apply to the reported recombinant preparation and assay conditions, not every protein construct or host.
No combined NcCAR–CHR cascade experiment was established in this check.
This note does not change frozen source-assertion counts or confer independent expert-review status.

records.reaction_context: Cinnamaldehyde reduction in an NADPH-dependent aldehyde-reductase assay, corresponding to the reduction direction of the reference reaction.
records.assay_readout: NADPH oxidation measured at 340 nm; cinnamaldehyde is directly included in the substrate activity and kinetic experiments.
records.product_confirmation: The inspected target-substrate kinetics establish activity with cinnamaldehyde. The described GC-MS product experiments use hexenal; they do not independently identify cinnamyl alcohol for this target assay. The table names cinnamaldehyde without independently resolving its E/Z form.
records.construct: At4g37980 open reading frame expressed as a C-terminal His-tagged recombinant protein in E. coli. Paper-listed RefSeq NP_195511.1 and the native database sequence match exactly.

conditions.description: 50 mM Tris-HCl and NADPH. This is the general enzyme-assay method, not a separately reported cinnamaldehyde pH optimum; the table does not specify a distinct buffer recipe for each kinetic series.

paper.title: Identification of a Hexenal Reductase That Modulates the Composition of Green Leaf Volatiles

limitations: Target-substrate activity is directly reported; separate chemical identification of cinnamyl alcohol was not established for this assay in the inspected material.
Cinnamaldehyde E/Z identity is not independently established by Table 2.
Evidence is assigned only to E023974 / At4g37980, not to all seven Arabidopsis candidates or another gene also called CAD7.
The relatively large reported Km uncertainty is retained; no precision or affinity superiority is inferred.
No combined NcCAR–CHR cascade experiment was established; the enzymes were measured under different conditions.
